hexextra.mishap.if_condition_count: An if condition must leave exactly one boolean on the stack, but it left %s (the two arguments go condition first, code block second -- swapping them causes this too)
hexextra.mishap.if_condition_not_bool: An if condition must leave a boolean, but it left %s (the two arguments go condition first, code block second -- swapping them causes this too)
hexextra.mishap.chain_already_has_else: This chain already has an else block; a chain can only have one
hexextra.mishap.replacement_has_else: A branch replacement must not carry an else block (branches are just a condition plus a body)
hexextra.mishap.duplicate_case: %s appears more than once as a switch case; every case constant must be unique
hexextra.mishap.case_not_constant: A case value must be a constant (number, boolean, null or pattern), but it was %s
hexextra.mishap.case_type_mismatch: This switch matches on %s, so it cannot take a case of a different type (that one was %s)
hexextra.mishap.switch_value_type_mismat: This switch matches on %s, but the value given was %s
hexextra.mishap.switch_type_mismatch: A %s switch and a %s switch cannot be merged
hexextra.mishap.switch_already_has_defau: This switch already has a default; a switch can only have one
hexextra.page.switch.rule: When run, a switch $(thing)consumes the value on top of the stack/$ and looks it up: the one matching case runs its block, and $(italic)nothing/$ falls through -- so no break is needed.$(br2)If nothing matches, the default runs; with no default either, nothing happens.$(br2)Matching is $(thing)exact/$, as with Java's switch, rather than tolerant.$(br2)A table matches exactly one type: putting a pattern case into a number table is an immediate error.
hexextra.page.switch.overload.title: Existing Patterns That Know Switch Tables
hexextra.page.switch.overload.intro: These patterns from Hexcasting itself follow the table's logic when handed a switch:
hexextra.page.switch.overload.add: Gathers two cases into a table, appends a case to a table, merges two tables (same type, at most one carrying a default), or turns an evaluatable iota into the default.
hexextra.page.switch.overload.remove_fro: Deletes case i; an out-of-range index returns the table unchanged.
hexextra.page.switch.overload.replace: Swaps case i for the given case.$(br2)An out-of-range index is an error, and the case must be of the table's type.
hexextra.page.switch.overload.index: Pulls case i out.$(br2)An out-of-range index gives null.
hexextra.page.switch.overload.abs: The number of cases. The default is $(italic)not/$ counted.
hexextra.category.patterns.desc: The patterns this addon brings to Hexcasting. They all build on what is already there, and they can be taken apart and put back together again.
hexextra.page.for_loop: Takes a loop count and an evaluatable iota off the stack, then runs that evaluatable iota that many times.$(br2)$(thing)Push the count first, the evaluatable iota second/$ -- so the evaluatable iota is on top.
hexextra.page.for_loop.rule: The loop itself costs no _media -- whatever is drawn inside the evaluatable iota settles its own cost.$(br2)A count of 0 or less does nothing; the cap is 10000.$(br2)The loop shares the stack with everything around it, so each pass picks up where the last one left off.$(br2)Drawing $(action)Charon's Gambit/$ inside the evaluatable iota breaks out early.
hexextra.page.if_chain: Takes a condition block and an evaluatable iota off the stack and ties the two into a conditional chain.$(br2)$(thing)Push the condition block first, the evaluatable iota second/$ -- so the evaluatable iota is on top. Swapping them raises no error; it merely looks like nothing happened.$(br2)This only puts the chain on the stack. Draw $(action)Hermes' Gambit/$ on it to run it.
hexextra.page.if_chain.rule: When run, each branch's condition is evaluated in turn.$(br2)A condition block must leave $(thing)exactly/$ one boolean on the stack, or the cast mishaps.$(br2)The first branch that comes up true runs its evaluatable iota and the rest are skipped; only when nothing matches does the else block run.$(br2)If a condition is false and no branch or else follows it, the whole chain simply does nothing -- that is normal.$(br2)To add more branches, use $(action)Additive Distillation/$.
hexextra.page.overload.intro.title: Existing Patterns That Know Chains
hexextra.page.overload.intro: These patterns belong to Hexcasting itself. Handed a $(thing)conditional chain/$ they follow the chain's logic, so their arguments differ from usual.$(br2)Their behaviour on plain lists is unaffected.
hexextra.page.overload.add: Joins two chains, or turns an evaluatable iota into the final else.$(br2)Errors if the first argument already has an else.
hexextra.page.overload.remove_from: Deletes branch i.$(br2)An out-of-range index returns the chain unchanged rather than erroring.
hexextra.page.overload.replace: Swaps branch i for another chain.$(br2)An out-of-range index is an error, and the replacement must not carry an else of its own.
hexextra.page.overload.index: Pulls branch i out, as a single-branch chain.$(br2)An out-of-range index gives null.
hexextra.page.overload.abs: The number of branches. The final else block is $(italic)not/$ counted.
hexextra.page.overload.splat: Spreads the chain out: every branch becomes a single-branch chain, and if the chain carries an else, one else-only chain is pushed last.
hexextra.page.overload.last_n_list: If the top n iotas are all conditional chains, gathers them into one in a single step -- like repeated addition.$(br2)Otherwise it keeps its usual behaviour of packing them into a list.
hexextra.page.switch: A switch table is built out of cases.$(br2)A case pairs a constant with the evaluatable iota to run when it matches. $(action)Case's Strategy/$ makes one, and $(action)Additive Distillation/$ either gathers cases into a table or appends one to an existing table.$(br2)The type a table matches on comes from its $(italic)first case/$; adding a case of another type is an immediate error.$(br2)A lone case is $(thing)raw material/$, not a runnable table -- drawing $(action)Hermes' Gambit/$ on it gives an unescaped-value mishap.
hexextra.page.case: Makes one case: the constant to match, plus the evaluatable iota to run when it matches.$(br2)$(thing)Push the constant first, the evaluatable iota second/$ -- so the evaluatable iota is on top.$(br2)The constant must be a number, boolean, null or pattern; anything else (list, entity, vector) is an immediate error.
hexextra.mishap.no_enclosing_loop: This pattern only works inside a loop
hexextra.page.for_down: Same as For's Strategy, only the index counts down. The first pass reports n-1, the last reports 0. Different from the reverse of a list: the body still runs in the same order.
hexextra.page.get_index: The current pass number, counting from 0.
hexextra.page.get_remaining: How many passes are left after this one. In a foreach, how many elements are still untouched.
hexextra.page.for_each: Runs the evaluatable iota once per element of the list.$(br2)Unlike Thoth, the element is not pushed onto the stack. Draw Current's Strategy inside the evaluatable iota to read it.
hexextra.page.get_current: The element being processed right now. Only works inside a foreach.
